question: Why do the divisions of power and its possessor become objects of worship?
premises: The divisions of power, its possessor, and so on come to be worshipped.
This begins from the first point where difference dissolves.
From that point each bears its own proper form.
inference: These divisions become worshippable because, from the threshold of dissolving difference, each manifests its own true form.
plain_english: Indeed, the divisions of power, its possessor, and so forth become worthy of worship, because from the very first point of the dissolution of difference each bears its own proper form.
